first.rationale: Current data shows both activation and onboarding completion declining 4-6% QoQ. Memory_31 demonstrated that signup simplification produced durable SMB activation lift, and memory_86 confirmed onboarding shortening improved completion rates. These are directly causal to the observed decline. While memory_73 indicates promotional pricing is effective for price-sensitive segments facing competitive pressure, that is a revenue-defense tactic that does not address the underlying product funnel deterioration. Simplifying onboarding targets the measurable gap (4% completion decline) and aligns with a proven lever (memory_31). Verifying memory_31 and memory_73 will confirm whether simplification remains our strongest lever relative to a price response, given the constraint of one experiment. Enterprise_sales_assist is orthogonal to the SMB activation crisis. Referral incentives work best on established cohorts, not on new acquisition. Activation messaging (memory_91) is promising but memory_86 shows structural onboarding improvements may compound it. Starting with onboarding simplification preserves optionality for follow-up messaging experiments while addressing the primary funnel constraint.

final.rationale: Verification confirms memory_31: signup simplification drove +9% activation and +4% qualified revenue on SMB with only -1% retention risk. Memory_73 verification reveals critical constraint: promotional pricing drives acquisition (+31%) but destroys cohort quality, with -12% retention and failure at renewal. This disqualifies promotional_pricing as a sustainable response to competitive pressure. Current situation shows activation down 6% and onboarding completion down 4% QoQ—both directly addressable by signup simplification, which has proven SMB-segment efficacy with durable retention. Enterprise_sales_assist does not address the SMB funnel crisis. Referral_incentives and activation_messaging are secondary optimization levers that could follow onboarding recovery. Simplifying onboarding is the only candidate that (1) directly targets observed metrics decline, (2) has verified positive impact on qualified revenue, (3) preserves retention health, and (4) aligns with stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. The competitive pricing threat is real, but matching it via discounting creates worse long-term damage (based on exp_73 evidence) than improving funnel quality and time-to-value.
